text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- At an informal meeting of European Union justice and interior ministers Danish justice minister Frank Jensen proposed Europol assists in investigating biker crime in Denmark, paving the way for closer police cooperation within EU.
--- Danes do not use Internet as much as their Nordic neighbours due to high Danish prices, a survey shows.

--- Danish Rail plans to offer free bus and taxi transport across the future Great Belt road-rail, tunnel-bridge fixed link for customers nervous about using the undersea tunnel when it opens for rail traffic this summer.

--- A growing number of Danes are taking out group life insurance policies. At present at least 2.5 million Danes have group life insurance policies while the number of individual life insurance policies grew by eight percent in 1996.

--- Telecoms group Tele Danmark's firing of 2,500 employees last week could cost it its reputation for being a pioneer in good staff relations, frightening off potential international investors, according to an expert report.
--- Denmark's largest institutional investor ATP and German Morgan Grenfell agree that Danish shares are cheap for international investors even though prices have been rising for some time.
